sourceHtml:
Every time a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server published in the AWS Agent Registry, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, gains a new tool or updates its schema, the registry record must be updated too. Without automated push-based sync, consumers discover stale metadata. For organizations managing multiple MCP servers across accounts, such a sync keeps catalog records current within an existing governance workflow.

In most enterprise deployments, a catalog’s value depends on its freshness. If a developer deploys a new tool on Monday, but the registry record still reflects last week’s schema, consumers lose trust in the catalog. Stale metadata directly reduces registry reliability, leading teams to inadvertently build dependencies on inaccurate information.

When an engineer adds a tool to an MCP server but forgets to update the catalog:

  • Consumers miss out on the new capability entirely.
  • Applications might call the tool using an outdated schema, causing unexpected runtime behavior or silent workflow deviations.

Multiplied across teams, this lack of automation erodes trust in the registry. Organizations ultimately fall back on ad hoc discovery mechanisms like hardcoded endpoints, informal knowledge sharing, and stale documentation.

In this post, we outline an event-driven architecture that automates these updates using AWS CloudTrail, Amazon EventBridge, and AWS Lambda.

Architecture overview

The following solution brings these services together into an event-driven pipeline that detects runtime changes and synchronizes them to the registry automatically.

The architecture supports both multi-account and single-account environments:

  • Single-account setup: For straightforward deployments, all components reside within Account A. Cross-account forwarding setup isn’t needed as events flow directly within Account A.
  • Multi-account setup: This involves two accounts where runtime events from Account B are securely forwarded to Account A.
    • Account A (registry account) owns the AWS Agent Registry, the Amazon EventBridge rule, the push-sync Lambda function, and CloudTrail logs.
    • Account B (MCP server account) hosts the MCP server runtime and the Amazon Cognito OAuth provider used for authentication.

The sample uses two accounts, but you can scale the architecture for multiple accounts, with Account A as the registry account and multiple AWS accounts similar to Account B for different MCP servers.

The following diagram shows the end-to-end event flow for an update to an MCP server in Account B. The captured event is forwarded to Account A, where a Lambda function queries the MCP server for its tools and updates the matching registry record.

Figure 1: End-to-end event flow for a cross-account MCP server update, from the CloudTrail event in Account B to the registry record update in Account A.

The architecture uses five AWS services:

  • AWS CloudTrail captures UpdateAgentRuntime API calls as management events.
  • Amazon EventBridge routes matching events to the Lambda function, with cross-account forwarding supported.
  • AWS Lambda queries the MCP server for its current tools, diffs against the registry, and updates the record if changed.
  • AWS Agent Registry stores MCP server records and their tool schemas as the central source of truth.
  • AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, brokers OAuth token exchanges securely, so the Lambda authenticates without storing secrets.

How it works: business logic flow

After it’s deployed, the pipeline runs the following end-to-end workflow:

  1. Trigger: A developer in Account B updates an MCP server, which calls the UpdateAgentRuntime API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and AWS CloudTrail captures the event.
  2. Route: Amazon EventBridge catches the CloudTrail event and forwards it to the central event bus in Account A.
  3. Parse: The sync Lambda in Account A extracts the runtime Amazon Resource Name (ARN) from the event payload and dynamically constructs the MCP server’s invocation URL. This is how it knows which server in Account B to query.
  4. Authenticate: The Lambda generates a secure OAuth bearer token through AgentCore Identity.
  5. Fetch: The Lambda calls the MCP server (initialize, then tools/list) to retrieve the latest tools information.
  6. Sync: The Lambda finds the matching registry record by its ARN, evaluates the differences, and updates the registry if the schema has changed.

This flow assumes that the Agent Registry in Account A already contains a pre-registered record for the MCP server (created during initial onboarding). The Lambda function in this sample updates existing records only. It doesn’t generate new ones.

This same flow works in a single-account setup where all resources (registry, Lambda, Amazon EventBridge rule, and MCP server) reside in one account. In that case, skip the cross-account forwarding step. Events flow directly within the same account’s Amazon EventBridge bus.

Technical walkthrough

This section walks through the workflow for a single MCP server update with two accounts as depicted in the architecture diagram.

The same flow executes independently for each server that emits an UpdateAgentRuntime event. The Lambda handles one event at a time, scaling naturally with the Amazon EventBridge invocation model.

Step 1: Event capture and routing for cross-account setup

When a developer deploys or updates an MCP server, the UpdateAgentRuntime API is called, either by the AgentCore CLI (agentcore deploy) or directly.

AWS CloudTrail records this as a management event in Account B, with a delivery delay of approximately 5–15 minutes. The event is then delivered to Account A’s default Amazon EventBridge bus.

For a cross-account setup, Account B’s Amazon EventBridge forwards matching events to Account A’s event bus through a cross-account rule.

The Amazon EventBridge rule target in Account A invokes the sync Lambda, passing the full CloudTrail event JSON as the input payload.

The Amazon EventBridge rule pattern:

{
  "source": ["aws.bedrock-agentcore"],
  "detail-type": ["API Call via AWS CloudTrail"],
  "detail": { "eventName": ["UpdateAgentRuntime"] }
}

The Lambda parses the runtime ARN from the event. It extracts the hosting Account ID and AWS Region to dynamically construct the target MCP server’s URL-encoded invocation endpoint.

# Extract the runtime ARN from the AWS CloudTrail event payload
def _extract_mcp_url(event):
    detail = event.get("detail", {})
    runtime_arn = detail.get("responseElements", {}).get("agentRuntimeArn", "")
    if not runtime_arn:
        return None, None
    # Parse the account ID from the ARN (5th colon-separated segment)
    arn_parts = runtime_arn.split(":")
    account_id = arn_parts[4] if len(arn_parts) > 4 else None
    region = detail.get("awsRegion", "us-west-2")
    # URL-encode the ARN and build the MCP invocation endpoint
    encoded_arn = runtime_arn.replace(":", "%3A").replace("/", "%2F")
    mcp_url = (f"https://bedrock-agentcore.{region}.amazonaws.com"
               f"/runtimes/{encoded_arn}/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT")
    return mcp_url, account_id

Step 3: Secure authentication with AgentCore Identity

The Lambda authenticates using a two-step identity flow. It exchanges its execution identity for a temporary workload token. The Lambda then trades this token for a scoped OAuth bearer token through the target account’s credential provider.

def get_bearer_token(account_id=None):
    """Get OAuth bearer token via AgentCore Identity credential provider.

    Two-step process:
    1. Get a workload access token from AgentCore Identity (identifies this Lambda)
    2. Use it to fetch an OAuth token from the credential provider (M2M flow)

    The credential provider stores the Cognito/OAuth config securely in AgentCore
    Identity, so no client secrets are needed in Lambda env vars.
    """
    acct = account_id or ""
    provider_name = os.environ.get(f"CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{acct}") or os.environ.get("CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER", "")
    scope_str = os.environ.get(f"CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_{acct}") or os.environ.get("CREDENTIAL_SCOPE", "")
    scopes = [s.strip() for s in scope_str.split(",") if s.strip()] if scope_str else []
    workload_name = os.environ.get("WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME", "")
    if not provider_name:
        raise ValueError(f"No CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER configured for account {acct}")
    if not workload_name:
        raise ValueError("WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME env var not set")
    region = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", "us-west-2")
    client = boto3.client("bedrock-agentcore", region_name=region)
    # Step 1: Get workload access token (identifies this Lambda as a trusted workload)
    wat_response = client.get_workload_access_token(
        workloadName=workload_name,
    )
    print(f"Workload access token response keys: {list(wat_response.keys())}")
    workload_token = wat_response.get("workloadAccessToken") or wat_response.get("accessToken", "")
    if not workload_token:
        raise ValueError(f"No access token in workload response: {list(wat_response.keys())}")
    # Step 2: Use workload token to get OAuth token from the credential provider
    response = client.get_resource_oauth2_token(
        workloadIdentityToken=workload_token,
        resourceCredentialProviderName=provider_name,
        oauth2Flow="M2M",
        scopes=scopes,
    )
    return response["accessToken"]

Credential providers are per-account (CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{ACCT_ID}), so one Lambda authenticates MCP servers across multiple accounts.

Step 4: Query the MCP server

Using standard MCP streamable-HTTP mechanics, the Lambda establishes an active session through an initialize request. After the session is active, it calls tools/list to fetch the complete array of currently exposed tools and schemas.

def call_tools_list(mcp_url, token):
    """Call the MCP server's initialize + tools/list methods and return the result.

    MCP streamable-http requires initialize before tools/list.
    The session_id from initialize is passed to tools/list if the server uses sessions.
    """
    # Validate URL scheme to prevent file:// or custom scheme access
    if not mcp_url.startswith("https://"):
        raise ValueError(f"Only HTTPS URLs are allowed, got: {mcp_url[:50]}")
    # Step 1: Initialize MCP session
    init_payload = {
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": "init-1",
        "method": "initialize",
        "params": {
            "protocolVersion": "2025-03-26",
            "capabilities": {},
            "clientInfo": {"name": "tool-sync-lambda", "version": "1.0.0"},
        },
    }
    init_resp = requests.post(
        mcp_url,
        json=init_payload,
        headers=_mcp_headers(token),
        timeout=30,
    )
    init_resp.raise_for_status()
    session_id = init_resp.headers.get("Mcp-Session-Id")
    init_result = _parse_sse_json(init_resp.text)
    print(f"MCP session initialized, session_id={session_id}")
    # Step 2: Call tools/list
    list_payload = {
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": "list-1",
        "method": "tools/list",
        "params": {},
    }
    list_resp = requests.post(
        mcp_url,
        json=list_payload,
        headers=_mcp_headers(token, session_id),
        timeout=30,
    )
    list_resp.raise_for_status()
    return _parse_sse_json(list_resp.text)

Step 5: Find the matching registry record

The Lambda queries the central Agent Registry to locate the corresponding record. It searches APPROVED records for one whose mcpServer.data contains the runtime ARN embedded during record creation (see the Deployment section).

# Decode the runtime ARN from the MCP URL for matching
def _find_record_by_mcp_url(client, registry_id, mcp_url):
    """Search registry records to find one whose server schema contains the runtime ARN.

    Tries three matching strategies:
    1. Decoded ARN (e.g. arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:...:runtime/TrimMCP-xxx)
    2. URL-encoded ARN (e.g. arn%3Aaws%3Abedrock-agentcore%3A...%2FTrimMCP-xxx)
    3. Full MCP URL match

    Returns:
        (record_id, full_record) tuple. Both None if no match found.
    """
    # Extract the runtime ARN from the MCP URL for matching
    # URL format: .../runtimes/arn%3A...%2Fruntime%2F<id>/invocations...
    # Decode to get: arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:region:account:runtime/id
    try:
        decoded_url = urllib.parse.unquote(mcp_url)
        # Extract just the runtime path: arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:...:runtime/xxx
        runtime_marker = "/runtimes/"
        idx = decoded_url.find(runtime_marker)
        if idx >= 0:
            runtime_arn = decoded_url[idx + len(runtime_marker) :].split("/invocations")[0]
        else:
            runtime_arn = None
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        runtime_arn = None
    records = client.list_registry_records(registryId=registry_id)
    record_list = records.get("registryRecords", [])
    print(f"Found {len(record_list)} registry records")
    for rec in record_list:
        record_id = rec.get("registryRecordId") or rec.get("recordId") or rec.get("id", "")
        record_name = rec.get("name", "?")
        record_status = rec.get("status", "?")
        print(f" Record: {record_id} | {record_name} | status={record_status} | keys={list(rec.keys())}")
        if not record_id:
            print(f" Warning: could not get record ID from: {list(rec.keys())}")
            continue
        if record_status == "DRAFT":
            print(f" Skipping DRAFT record {record_id} ({record_name}) — must be APPROVED first")
            continue
        try:
            full = client.get_registry_record(
                registryId=registry_id,
                recordId=record_id,
            )
            descriptors = full.get("descriptors", {})
            mcp_desc = descriptors.get("mcpServer", {})
            inline = mcp_desc.get("data", "")
            # Match on runtime ARN (decoded or encoded) in the server schema
            if runtime_arn and runtime_arn in inline:
                print(f"Found matching record (by ARN): {record_id} ({rec.get('name', '?')})")
                return record_id, full
            # Also check URL-encoded ARN
            encoded_arn = runtime_arn.replace(":", "%3A").replace("/", "%2F") if runtime_arn else None
            if encoded_arn and encoded_arn in inline:
                print(f"Found matching record (by encoded ARN): {record_id} ({rec.get('name', '?')})")
                return record_id, full
            if mcp_url in inline or urllib.parse.unquote(mcp_url).replace("?qualifier=DEFAULT", "") in inline:
                print(f"Found matching record (by URL): {record_id} ({rec.get('name', '?')})")
                return record_id, full
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"Error checking record {record_id}: {e}")
            continue
    print(f"No matching record found among {len(record_list)} records.")
    print(f" Looking for runtime ARN: {runtime_arn}")
    print(f" Looking for MCP URL: {mcp_url}")
    return None, None

Step 6: Diff and update

To minimize unnecessary writes, tool lists are normalized (sorted by name, compared using name + description + inputSchema). The registry update only fires when a change is detected. If the schemas differ, the Lambda logs the exact additions or removals and pushes the fresh definitions to the registry record.

# Normalize tool definitions for comparison (sort by name, extract key fields)
def _normalize_tools(tools):
    """Normalize tool list for comparison — extract name, description, inputSchema."""
    normalized = []
    for t in sorted(tools, key=lambda x: x.get("name", "")):
        normalized.append(
            {
                "name": t.get("name", ""),
                "description": t.get("description", ""),
                "inputSchema": t.get("inputSchema", {}),
            }
        )
    return normalized

def _normalize_tools(tools):
    """Normalize tool list for comparison — extract name, description, inputSchema."""
    normalized = []
    for t in sorted(tools, key=lambda x: x.get("name", "")):
        normalized.append(
            {
                "name": t.get("name", ""),
                "description": t.get("description", ""),
                "inputSchema": t.get("inputSchema", {}),
            }
        )
    return normalized

def sync_registry_if_changed(mcp_tools, mcp_url):
    """Compare MCP server tools with AWS Agent Registry record tools. Update only if different.

    Steps:
    1. Find the AWS Agent Registry record matching this MCP server's URL
    2. Extract existing tools from the record's tools.inlineContent
    3. Normalize both tool lists (sort by name, compare name/description/inputSchema)
    4. If identical → skip update
    5. If different → log the diff and update the registry record

    Returns:
        dict with 'action' key: 'no_change', 'updated', or 'skipped'
    """
    registry_id = os.environ["REGISTRY_ID"]
    client = _get_registry_client()
    # Find the matching record
    record_id, full_record = _find_record_by_mcp_url(client, registry_id, mcp_url)
    if not record_id:
        print(f"No matching registry record found for {mcp_url}")
        return {"action": "skipped", "reason": "no matching record"}
    # Get current tools from registry
    registry_tools = _get_registry_tools_from_record(full_record)
    # Compare normalized tool lists
    mcp_normalized = _normalize_tools(mcp_tools)
    registry_normalized = _normalize_tools(registry_tools)
    if mcp_normalized == registry_normalized:
        print(f"No change detected. Registry record {record_id} is up to date ({len(registry_tools)} tools).")
        return {
            "action": "no_change",
            "record_id": record_id,
            "tool_count": len(registry_tools),
        }
    # Tools differ — update the registry
    print(f"Change detected! Registry has {len(registry_tools)} tools, MCP server has {len(mcp_tools)} tools.")
    # Log the diff
    mcp_names = {t["name"] for t in mcp_normalized}
    reg_names = {t["name"] for t in registry_normalized}
    added = mcp_names - reg_names
    removed = reg_names - mcp_names
    if added:
        print(f" Added: {added}")
    if removed:
        print(f" Removed: {removed}")
    if not added and not removed:
        print(" Tool definitions changed (same names, different schemas/descriptions)")
    tool_schema_content = json.dumps({"tools": mcp_tools})
    client.update_registry_record(
        registryId=registry_id,
        recordId=record_id,
        descriptors={
            "optionalValue": {
                "mcpServer": {
                    "optionalValue": {
                        "additionalData": {
                            "optionalValue": {
                                "tools": {
                                    "optionalValue": {
                                        "data": {
                                            "optionalValue": tool_schema_content,
                                        },
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        },
    )
    print(f"Updated registry record {record_id} in registry {registry_id}")
    return {
        "action": "updated",
        "record_id": record_id,
        "old_count": len(registry_tools),
        "new_count": len(mcp_tools),
    }

Governance and approval workflow

AWS Agent Registry enforces a governance lifecycle on each record: Draft -> Pending Approval -> Approved (or Rejected/Deprecated). Administrators configure approval settings at the registry level. These settings control what gets published, who reviews it, and whether records require manual approval before becoming discoverable. Only records in Approved status are visible to consumers through search, catalog browsing, or the registry’s MCP endpoint.

When the Lambda updates a record with new tool definitions, the record automatically reverts to Draft status. Consumers continue to see the previously approved version. A curator or administrator must then approve the update before the new metadata becomes discoverable. This way the automated updates cannot bypass organizational review, and administrators retain full control over what is exposed to consumers.

Deployment

The following table outlines steps in the automation pipeline:

Step Description
Define configuration Region, Lambda name, registry ID, and MCP server ARN
Create and approve registry record Register the MCP server entry and move it to APPROVED
Provision AgentCore Identity Create workload identity and OAuth2 credential providers
Deploy Lambda function Create IAM execution role, package handler, deploy function
Create Amazon EventBridge rule Route UpdateAgentRuntime events to the Lambda
Cross-account forwarding (optional) Forward runtime events from remote accounts

Prerequisites

Before deploying this solution, verify that the following are in place:

  • An AWS account with permissions to create Lambda functions, Amazon EventBridge rules, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles, and Agent Registry resources.
  • AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) configured with credentials to access all the services used in the sample. For more information, see Getting started with the AWS CLI.
  • Python 3.12 runtime.
  • An existing AWS Agent Registry with at least one MCP server record (created during initial onboarding; instructions to create the record are provided in the Deployment section).
  • An MCP server deployed on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime.
  • An AgentCore Identity workload identity and OAuth2 credential providers configured for each MCP server account (see sample repository for setup).
  • For multi-account setups, cross-account Amazon EventBridge permissions between Account B and Account A.

Organizations often use multiple accounts, where the registry is in one account but the MCP servers are in others. This sample outlines the multi-account scenario, which you can convert to a single-account scenario by following the instructions.

Creating the registry record

In this sample, before the sync pipeline can work, a registry record must exist with the runtime ARN explicitly embedded in its server schema. You can use the following code to create the registry record and include the runtime ARN in the record’s mcpServer.data field. This is what the Lambda matches against to correlate AWS CloudTrail events to records:

# The websiteUrl contains the MCP server invocation URL with the encoded
# runtime ARN: this is what the Lambda matches against later.
encoded_arn = MCP_RUNTIME_ARN.replace(":", "%3A").replace("/", "%2F")
mcp_server_url = (
    f"https://bedrock-agentcore.{AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com"
    f"/runtimes/{encoded_arn}/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT"
)
server_schema = json.dumps({
    "name": MCP_SERVER_NAME,
    "description": MCP_SERVER_DESCRIPTION,
    "websiteUrl": mcp_server_url,
})
registry_cp.create_registry_record(
    registryId=REGISTRY_ID,
    name=MCP_SERVER_NAME,
    description=MCP_SERVER_DESCRIPTION,
    recordType="MCP",
    recordVersion="1.0",
    descriptors={"mcpServer": {"data": server_schema}}
)

Approving the record

The Lambda only syncs to APPROVED records.

After making the update, the registry record is in the DRAFT stage. It must move through the governance workflow for the change to be discoverable.

# Submit for approval (DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL)
registry_cp.submit_registry_record_for_approval(
    registryId=REGISTRY_ID,
    recordId=RECORD_ID,
)
# Approve (PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED)
registry_cp.update_registry_record_status(
    registryId=REGISTRY_ID,
    recordId=RECORD_ID,
    status="APPROVED",
)

Lambda environment variables

To maintain a strong security posture, zero client secrets are stored in the Lambda environment variables. The function relies entirely on mapping environment variables to reference runtime workload identities, provider names, and permission scopes.

# No client secrets here. Only provider names and scopes.
# The Lambda uses WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME to get a workload token,
# then CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{ACCT} to fetch the OAuth token.
env_vars = {
    "REGISTRY_ID": REGISTRY_ID,
    "WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME": WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME,
}
for acct_id, config in ACCOUNT_CONFIGS.items():
    env_vars[f"CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{acct_id}"] = config["provider_name"]
    env_vars[f"CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_{acct_id}"] = config.get("scope", "")

Amazon EventBridge rule

This rule acts as the pipeline trigger, listening for UpdateAgentRuntime management events within the local account or arriving from cross-account Amazon EventBridge bus forwarders:

# Match UpdateAgentRuntime events from AgentCore.
# Fires when any runtime is created or updated in this account
# (or forwarded from a cross-account EventBridge bus).
event_pattern = {
    "source": ["aws.bedrock-agentcore"],
    "detail-type": ["API Call via AWS CloudTrail"],
    "detail": {"eventName": ["UpdateAgentRuntime"]}
}
events_client.put_rule(
    Name=f"{LAMBDA_NAME}-trigger",
    EventPattern=json.dumps(event_pattern),
    State="ENABLED",
)

Clean up

To avoid ongoing charges, delete the following resources when you are done:

  • Lambda function – Delete the push-sync Lambda and its IAM execution role.
  • Amazon EventBridge rule – Delete the rule and its Lambda target.
  • AgentCore Identity – Delete the workload identity and OAuth2 credential providers.
  • Registry record – Delete or deprecate the test MCP server record.
  • Registry – Delete the registry if it was created solely for testing.
  • (Multi-account) Remove the cross-account Amazon EventBridge rule and resource policy in Account B.

You can find the cleanup code in the sample repository.

Known limitations and future improvements

The sample code outlined here (and in the full sample) can be extended in several ways:

  • Automatic registration of new MCP servers – Currently, a matching registry record must already exist. A future enhancement could automatically create a record when a previously unknown MCP server is detected for the first time.
  • Manual “force sync” trigger – For time-sensitive deployments, an on-demand invocation path through Amazon API Gateway or a CLI command can serve changes outside the regular CloudTrail delivery flow.
  • Cold-start resilience – If an MCP server is cold and returns zero tools, the Lambda currently doesn’t retry. Adding exponential backoff and skipping the update when the tool count is zero would improve reliability.

Conclusion

The AWS Agent Registry gives organizations a governed, discoverable catalog for their AI agents and MCP servers.

The push-sync Lambda pattern closes the freshness gap: when a server change is detected, the registry record is updated automatically and securely, within the constraints described in the Known limitations section. Updates revert the record to DRAFT status and must pass through the approval workflow before becoming discoverable again.

As your agent fleet grows from a handful to hundreds of MCP servers, this pattern keeps your registry as the single source of truth, consistently fresh and reviewed.

Get started

The full implementation (Lambda code, deployment script, and architecture diagram) is available as a ready-to-deploy sample. To deploy the solution in your environment, clone the repository and follow the deployment steps in the README.

每当发布在 AWS Agent Registry（Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项功能）中的模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器新增工具或更新其架构时，注册表记录也必须随之更新。如果没有基于推送的自动同步，使用方发现的就会是过时的元数据。对于跨账户管理多个 MCP 服务器的组织，这种同步可以在现有治理工作流内保持目录记录的及时更新。

在大多数企业部署中，目录的价值取决于其信息是否及时更新。如果开发者在周一部署了一个新工具，但注册表记录仍然反映上周的架构，使用方就会对目录失去信任。过时的元数据会直接降低注册表的可靠性，导致团队在不知不觉中基于不准确的信息构建依赖关系。

当工程师向 MCP 服务器添加工具，却忘记更新目录时：

  • 使用方会完全错过这项新功能。
  • 应用程序可能使用过时的架构调用该工具，导致意外的运行时行为或无声的工作流偏差。

当这种缺乏自动化的情况在多个团队中反复出现时，就会削弱大家对注册表的信任。组织最终会退回到临时性的发现机制，例如硬编码端点、非正式的知识分享和过时的文档。

本文将介绍一种事件驱动架构，使用 AWS CloudTrail、Amazon EventBridge 和 AWS Lambda 自动完成这些更新。

架构概览

以下解决方案将这些服务整合为一条事件驱动流水线，用于检测运行时变更并自动将其同步到注册表。

该架构同时支持多账户和单账户环境：

  • 单账户设置：对于简单的部署，所有组件都位于账户 A 中。由于事件直接在账户 A 内流转，因此无需设置跨账户转发。
  • Multi-account setup: This involves two accounts where runtime events from Account B are securely forwarded to Account A.
    • 账户 A（注册表账户）拥有 AWS Agent Registry、Amazon EventBridge 规则、推送同步 Lambda 函数和 CloudTrail 日志。
    • 账户 B（MCP 服务器账户）托管 MCP 服务器运行时以及用于身份验证的 Amazon Cognito OAuth 提供程序。

示例使用两个账户，但你可以将此架构扩展到多个账户，由账户 A 作为注册表账户，并使用多个类似账户 B 的 AWS 账户托管不同的 MCP 服务器。

下图展示了账户 B 中 MCP 服务器更新的端到端事件流。捕获的事件会转发到账户 A，由其中的 Lambda 函数查询 MCP 服务器的工具并更新匹配的注册表记录。

图 1：跨账户 MCP 服务器更新的端到端事件流，从账户 B 中的 CloudTrail 事件到账户 A 中的注册表记录更新。

该架构使用五项 AWS 服务：

  • AWS CloudTrail 将 UpdateAgentRuntime API 调用捕获为管理事件。
  • Amazon EventBridge 将匹配的事件路由到 Lambda 函数，并支持跨账户转发。
  • AWS Lambda 查询 MCP 服务器的当前工具，与注册表进行差异比较，并在发生变更时更新记录。
  • AWS Agent Registry 存储 MCP 服务器记录及其工具架构，作为集中的权威信息源。
  • AgentCore Identity 是 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项功能，可安全地代理 OAuth 令牌交换，使 Lambda 无需存储密钥即可完成身份验证。

工作原理：业务逻辑流程

部署完成后，流水线会运行以下端到端工作流：

  1. 触发：账户 B 中的开发者更新 MCP 服务器，从而调用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 中的 UpdateAgentRuntime API，AWS CloudTrail 随后捕获该事件。
  2. 路由：Amazon EventBridge 捕获 CloudTrail 事件，并将其转发到账户 A 中的中央事件总线。
  3. 解析：账户 A 中的同步 Lambda 从事件负载中提取运行时的 Amazon 资源名称（ARN），并动态构造 MCP 服务器的调用 URL。它通过这种方式确定要查询账户 B 中的哪台服务器。
  4. 身份验证：Lambda 通过 AgentCore Identity 生成安全的 OAuth 持有者令牌。
  5. 获取：Lambda 调用 MCP 服务器（先调用 initialize，再调用 tools/list），以检索最新的工具信息。
  6. 同步：Lambda 根据 ARN 查找匹配的注册表记录，评估差异，并在架构发生变化时更新注册表。

此流程假设账户 A 中的 Agent Registry 已包含该 MCP 服务器的预注册记录（在初始接入时创建）。本示例中的 Lambda 函数仅更新现有记录，不会创建新记录。

同一流程也适用于单账户设置，其中所有资源（注册表、Lambda、Amazon EventBridge 规则和 MCP 服务器）都位于同一个账户中。在这种情况下，跳过跨账户转发步骤即可。事件会直接在同一账户的 Amazon EventBridge 总线内流转。

技术详解

本节将按照架构图所示，介绍两个账户下单次 MCP 服务器更新的工作流程。

对于每台发出 UpdateAgentRuntime 事件的服务器，同一流程都会独立执行。Lambda 每次处理一个事件，并随 Amazon EventBridge 的调用模式自然扩展。

步骤 1：跨账户设置中的事件捕获与路由

当开发者部署或更新 MCP 服务器时，AgentCore CLI（agentcore deploy）会调用 UpdateAgentRuntime API，也可以直接调用该 API。

AWS CloudTrail 会在账户 B 中将其记录为管理事件，投递延迟约为 5–15 分钟。随后，该事件会被投递到账户 A 的默认 Amazon EventBridge 总线。

对于跨账户设置，账户 B 的 Amazon EventBridge 会通过跨账户规则，将匹配的事件转发到账户 A 的事件总线。

账户 A 中的 Amazon EventBridge 规则目标会调用同步 Lambda，并将完整的 CloudTrail 事件 JSON 作为输入负载传入。

Amazon EventBridge 规则模式：

{
  "source": ["aws.bedrock-agentcore"],
  "detail-type": ["API Call via AWS CloudTrail"],
  "detail": { "eventName": ["UpdateAgentRuntime"] }
}

Lambda 从事件中解析运行时 ARN，并提取托管账户 ID 和 AWS 区域，以动态构造经过 URL 编码的目标 MCP 服务器调用端点。

# Extract the runtime ARN from the AWS CloudTrail event payload
def _extract_mcp_url(event):
    detail = event.get("detail", {})
    runtime_arn = detail.get("responseElements", {}).get("agentRuntimeArn", "")
    if not runtime_arn:
        return None, None
    # Parse the account ID from the ARN (5th colon-separated segment)
    arn_parts = runtime_arn.split(":")
    account_id = arn_parts[4] if len(arn_parts) > 4 else None
    region = detail.get("awsRegion", "us-west-2")
    # URL-encode the ARN and build the MCP invocation endpoint
    encoded_arn = runtime_arn.replace(":", "%3A").replace("/", "%2F")
    mcp_url = (f"https://bedrock-agentcore.{region}.amazonaws.com"
               f"/runtimes/{encoded_arn}/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT")
    return mcp_url, account_id

步骤 3：使用 AgentCore Identity 进行安全身份验证

Lambda 使用两步身份流程进行身份验证。它先用自己的执行身份换取临时工作负载令牌，再通过目标账户的凭证提供程序，将该令牌换取为具有特定权限范围的 OAuth 持有者令牌。

def get_bearer_token(account_id=None):
    """Get OAuth bearer token via AgentCore Identity credential provider.

    Two-step process:
    1. Get a workload access token from AgentCore Identity (identifies this Lambda)
    2. Use it to fetch an OAuth token from the credential provider (M2M flow)

    The credential provider stores the Cognito/OAuth config securely in AgentCore
    Identity, so no client secrets are needed in Lambda env vars.
    """
    acct = account_id or ""
    provider_name = os.environ.get(f"CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{acct}") or os.environ.get("CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER", "")
    scope_str = os.environ.get(f"CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_{acct}") or os.environ.get("CREDENTIAL_SCOPE", "")
    scopes = [s.strip() for s in scope_str.split(",") if s.strip()] if scope_str else []
    workload_name = os.environ.get("WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME", "")
    if not provider_name:
        raise ValueError(f"No CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER configured for account {acct}")
    if not workload_name:
        raise ValueError("WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME env var not set")
    region = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", "us-west-2")
    client = boto3.client("bedrock-agentcore", region_name=region)
    # Step 1: Get workload access token (identifies this Lambda as a trusted workload)
    wat_response = client.get_workload_access_token(
        workloadName=workload_name,
    )
    print(f"Workload access token response keys: {list(wat_response.keys())}")
    workload_token = wat_response.get("workloadAccessToken") or wat_response.get("accessToken", "")
    if not workload_token:
        raise ValueError(f"No access token in workload response: {list(wat_response.keys())}")
    # Step 2: Use workload token to get OAuth token from the credential provider
    response = client.get_resource_oauth2_token(
        workloadIdentityToken=workload_token,
        resourceCredentialProviderName=provider_name,
        oauth2Flow="M2M",
        scopes=scopes,
    )
    return response["accessToken"]

凭证提供程序按账户设置（CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{ACCT_ID}），因此一个 Lambda 即可对多个账户中的 MCP 服务器进行身份验证。

步骤 4：查询 MCP 服务器

Lambda 使用标准 MCP 流式 HTTP 机制，通过 initialize 请求建立活动会话。会话激活后，它会调用 tools/list，获取当前对外提供的工具及其架构的完整数组。

def call_tools_list(mcp_url, token):
    """Call the MCP server's initialize + tools/list methods and return the result.

    MCP streamable-http requires initialize before tools/list.
    The session_id from initialize is passed to tools/list if the server uses sessions.
    """
    # Validate URL scheme to prevent file:// or custom scheme access
    if not mcp_url.startswith("https://"):
        raise ValueError(f"Only HTTPS URLs are allowed, got: {mcp_url[:50]}")
    # Step 1: Initialize MCP session
    init_payload = {
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": "init-1",
        "method": "initialize",
        "params": {
            "protocolVersion": "2025-03-26",
            "capabilities": {},
            "clientInfo": {"name": "tool-sync-lambda", "version": "1.0.0"},
        },
    }
    init_resp = requests.post(
        mcp_url,
        json=init_payload,
        headers=_mcp_headers(token),
        timeout=30,
    )
    init_resp.raise_for_status()
    session_id = init_resp.headers.get("Mcp-Session-Id")
    init_result = _parse_sse_json(init_resp.text)
    print(f"MCP session initialized, session_id={session_id}")
    # Step 2: Call tools/list
    list_payload = {
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": "list-1",
        "method": "tools/list",
        "params": {},
    }
    list_resp = requests.post(
        mcp_url,
        json=list_payload,
        headers=_mcp_headers(token, session_id),
        timeout=30,
    )
    list_resp.raise_for_status()
    return _parse_sse_json(list_resp.text)

步骤 5：查找匹配的注册表记录

Lambda 查询中央 Agent Registry，定位对应记录。它会在 APPROVED 状态的记录中，搜索 mcpServer.data 包含创建记录时嵌入的运行时 ARN 的记录（参见“部署”部分）。

# Decode the runtime ARN from the MCP URL for matching
def _find_record_by_mcp_url(client, registry_id, mcp_url):
    """Search registry records to find one whose server schema contains the runtime ARN.

    Tries three matching strategies:
    1. Decoded ARN (e.g. arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:...:runtime/TrimMCP-xxx)
    2. URL-encoded ARN (e.g. arn%3Aaws%3Abedrock-agentcore%3A...%2FTrimMCP-xxx)
    3. Full MCP URL match

    Returns:
        (record_id, full_record) tuple. Both None if no match found.
    """
    # Extract the runtime ARN from the MCP URL for matching
    # URL format: .../runtimes/arn%3A...%2Fruntime%2F<id>/invocations...
    # Decode to get: arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:region:account:runtime/id
    try:
        decoded_url = urllib.parse.unquote(mcp_url)
        # Extract just the runtime path: arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:...:runtime/xxx
        runtime_marker = "/runtimes/"
        idx = decoded_url.find(runtime_marker)
        if idx >= 0:
            runtime_arn = decoded_url[idx + len(runtime_marker) :].split("/invocations")[0]
        else:
            runtime_arn = None
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        runtime_arn = None
    records = client.list_registry_records(registryId=registry_id)
    record_list = records.get("registryRecords", [])
    print(f"Found {len(record_list)} registry records")
    for rec in record_list:
        record_id = rec.get("registryRecordId") or rec.get("recordId") or rec.get("id", "")
        record_name = rec.get("name", "?")
        record_status = rec.get("status", "?")
        print(f" Record: {record_id} | {record_name} | status={record_status} | keys={list(rec.keys())}")
        if not record_id:
            print(f" Warning: could not get record ID from: {list(rec.keys())}")
            continue
        if record_status == "DRAFT":
            print(f" Skipping DRAFT record {record_id} ({record_name}) — must be APPROVED first")
            continue
        try:
            full = client.get_registry_record(
                registryId=registry_id,
                recordId=record_id,
            )
            descriptors = full.get("descriptors", {})
            mcp_desc = descriptors.get("mcpServer", {})
            inline = mcp_desc.get("data", "")
            # Match on runtime ARN (decoded or encoded) in the server schema
            if runtime_arn and runtime_arn in inline:
                print(f"Found matching record (by ARN): {record_id} ({rec.get('name', '?')})")
                return record_id, full
            # Also check URL-encoded ARN
            encoded_arn = runtime_arn.replace(":", "%3A").replace("/", "%2F") if runtime_arn else None
            if encoded_arn and encoded_arn in inline:
                print(f"Found matching record (by encoded ARN): {record_id} ({rec.get('name', '?')})")
                return record_id, full
            if mcp_url in inline or urllib.parse.unquote(mcp_url).replace("?qualifier=DEFAULT", "") in inline:
                print(f"Found matching record (by URL): {record_id} ({rec.get('name', '?')})")
                return record_id, full
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"Error checking record {record_id}: {e}")
            continue
    print(f"No matching record found among {len(record_list)} records.")
    print(f" Looking for runtime ARN: {runtime_arn}")
    print(f" Looking for MCP URL: {mcp_url}")
    return None, None

步骤 6：比较差异并更新

为尽量减少不必要的写入，工具列表会经过规范化处理（按名称排序，并使用 name + description + inputSchema 进行比较）。只有检测到变更时才会触发注册表更新。如果架构不同，Lambda 会记录具体的新增或删除项，并将最新定义推送到注册表记录。

# Normalize tool definitions for comparison (sort by name, extract key fields)
def _normalize_tools(tools):
    """Normalize tool list for comparison — extract name, description, inputSchema."""
    normalized = []
    for t in sorted(tools, key=lambda x: x.get("name", "")):
        normalized.append(
            {
                "name": t.get("name", ""),
                "description": t.get("description", ""),
                "inputSchema": t.get("inputSchema", {}),
            }
        )
    return normalized

def _normalize_tools(tools):
    """Normalize tool list for comparison — extract name, description, inputSchema."""
    normalized = []
    for t in sorted(tools, key=lambda x: x.get("name", "")):
        normalized.append(
            {
                "name": t.get("name", ""),
                "description": t.get("description", ""),
                "inputSchema": t.get("inputSchema", {}),
            }
        )
    return normalized

def sync_registry_if_changed(mcp_tools, mcp_url):
    """Compare MCP server tools with AWS Agent Registry record tools. Update only if different.

    Steps:
    1. Find the AWS Agent Registry record matching this MCP server's URL
    2. Extract existing tools from the record's tools.inlineContent
    3. Normalize both tool lists (sort by name, compare name/description/inputSchema)
    4. If identical → skip update
    5. If different → log the diff and update the registry record

    Returns:
        dict with 'action' key: 'no_change', 'updated', or 'skipped'
    """
    registry_id = os.environ["REGISTRY_ID"]
    client = _get_registry_client()
    # Find the matching record
    record_id, full_record = _find_record_by_mcp_url(client, registry_id, mcp_url)
    if not record_id:
        print(f"No matching registry record found for {mcp_url}")
        return {"action": "skipped", "reason": "no matching record"}
    # Get current tools from registry
    registry_tools = _get_registry_tools_from_record(full_record)
    # Compare normalized tool lists
    mcp_normalized = _normalize_tools(mcp_tools)
    registry_normalized = _normalize_tools(registry_tools)
    if mcp_normalized == registry_normalized:
        print(f"No change detected. Registry record {record_id} is up to date ({len(registry_tools)} tools).")
        return {
            "action": "no_change",
            "record_id": record_id,
            "tool_count": len(registry_tools),
        }
    # Tools differ — update the registry
    print(f"Change detected! Registry has {len(registry_tools)} tools, MCP server has {len(mcp_tools)} tools.")
    # Log the diff
    mcp_names = {t["name"] for t in mcp_normalized}
    reg_names = {t["name"] for t in registry_normalized}
    added = mcp_names - reg_names
    removed = reg_names - mcp_names
    if added:
        print(f" Added: {added}")
    if removed:
        print(f" Removed: {removed}")
    if not added and not removed:
        print(" Tool definitions changed (same names, different schemas/descriptions)")
    tool_schema_content = json.dumps({"tools": mcp_tools})
    client.update_registry_record(
        registryId=registry_id,
        recordId=record_id,
        descriptors={
            "optionalValue": {
                "mcpServer": {
                    "optionalValue": {
                        "additionalData": {
                            "optionalValue": {
                                "tools": {
                                    "optionalValue": {
                                        "data": {
                                            "optionalValue": tool_schema_content,
                                        },
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        },
    )
    print(f"Updated registry record {record_id} in registry {registry_id}")
    return {
        "action": "updated",
        "record_id": record_id,
        "old_count": len(registry_tools),
        "new_count": len(mcp_tools),
    }

治理与审批工作流

AWS Agent Registry 对每条记录实施治理生命周期：草稿 -> 待审批 -> 已批准（或已拒绝/已弃用）。管理员在注册表级别配置审批设置。这些设置控制哪些内容会被发布、由谁审核，以及记录是否需要经过人工审批才能被发现。只有处于“已批准”状态的记录，使用方才能通过搜索、目录浏览或注册表的 MCP 端点看到。

当 Lambda 使用新的工具定义更新记录时，该记录会自动回到“草稿”状态。使用方仍会看到之前已批准的版本。随后，目录维护人员或管理员必须批准此次更新，新的元数据才能被发现。这样，自动更新就无法绕过组织审核，管理员也能完全掌控向使用方公开的内容。

部署

下表概述了自动化流水线中的步骤：

步骤 说明
定义配置 区域、Lambda 名称、注册表 ID 和 MCP 服务器 ARN
创建并批准注册表记录 注册 MCP 服务器条目，并将其状态设为 APPROVED
配置 AgentCore Identity 资源 创建工作负载身份和 OAuth2 凭证提供程序
部署 Lambda 函数 创建 IAM 执行角色、打包处理程序、部署函数
创建 Amazon EventBridge 规则 将 UpdateAgentRuntime 事件路由到 Lambda
跨账户转发（可选） 从远程账户转发运行时事件

前提条件

部署此解决方案之前，请确认已具备以下条件：

  • 一个具有创建 Lambda 函数、Amazon EventBridge 规则、AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）角色及 Agent Registry 资源权限的 AWS 账户。
  • 已配置凭证的 AWS Command Line Interface（AWS CLI），可访问示例中使用的所有服务。有关更多信息，请参阅开始使用 AWS CLI。
  • Python 3.12 运行时。
  • 一个现有的 AWS Agent Registry，其中至少包含一条 MCP 服务器记录（在初始接入时创建；创建记录的说明见“部署”部分）。
  • 一台部署在 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 运行时上的 MCP 服务器。
  • 为每个 MCP 服务器账户配置的 AgentCore Identity 工作负载身份和 OAuth2 凭证提供程序（设置方法见示例代码仓库）。
  • 对于多账户设置，需具备账户 B 与账户 A 之间的跨账户 Amazon EventBridge 权限。

组织通常使用多个账户，注册表位于一个账户中，而 MCP 服务器位于其他账户中。本示例介绍多账户场景，你可以按照说明将其转换为单账户场景。

创建注册表记录

在本示例中，同步流水线要正常工作，必须先存在一条在服务器架构中明确嵌入运行时 ARN 的注册表记录。你可以使用以下代码创建注册表记录，并将运行时 ARN 写入记录的 mcpServer.data 字段。Lambda 会通过匹配该字段，将 AWS CloudTrail 事件与记录关联起来：

# The websiteUrl contains the MCP server invocation URL with the encoded
# runtime ARN: this is what the Lambda matches against later.
encoded_arn = MCP_RUNTIME_ARN.replace(":", "%3A").replace("/", "%2F")
mcp_server_url = (
    f"https://bedrock-agentcore.{AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com"
    f"/runtimes/{encoded_arn}/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT"
)
server_schema = json.dumps({
    "name": MCP_SERVER_NAME,
    "description": MCP_SERVER_DESCRIPTION,
    "websiteUrl": mcp_server_url,
})
registry_cp.create_registry_record(
    registryId=REGISTRY_ID,
    name=MCP_SERVER_NAME,
    description=MCP_SERVER_DESCRIPTION,
    recordType="MCP",
    recordVersion="1.0",
    descriptors={"mcpServer": {"data": server_schema}}
)

批准记录

Lambda 仅同步到 APPROVED 状态的记录。

更新完成后，注册表记录处于 DRAFT 阶段。它必须经过治理工作流，此次变更才能被发现。

# Submit for approval (DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL)
registry_cp.submit_registry_record_for_approval(
    registryId=REGISTRY_ID,
    recordId=RECORD_ID,
)
# Approve (PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED)
registry_cp.update_registry_record_status(
    registryId=REGISTRY_ID,
    recordId=RECORD_ID,
    status="APPROVED",
)

Lambda 环境变量

为保持较高的安全水平，Lambda 环境变量中不存储任何客户端密钥。该函数完全依靠环境变量映射来引用运行时工作负载身份、提供程序名称和权限范围。

# No client secrets here. Only provider names and scopes.
# The Lambda uses WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME to get a workload token,
# then CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{ACCT} to fetch the OAuth token.
env_vars = {
    "REGISTRY_ID": REGISTRY_ID,
    "WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME": WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_NAME,
}
for acct_id, config in ACCOUNT_CONFIGS.items():
    env_vars[f"CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_{acct_id}"] = config["provider_name"]
    env_vars[f"CREDENTIAL_SCOPE_{acct_id}"] = config.get("scope", "")

Amazon EventBridge 规则

该规则作为流水线的触发器，监听本地账户中的 UpdateAgentRuntime 管理事件，或通过跨账户 Amazon EventBridge 总线转发器传入的此类事件：

# Match UpdateAgentRuntime events from AgentCore.
# Fires when any runtime is created or updated in this account
# (or forwarded from a cross-account EventBridge bus).
event_pattern = {
    "source": ["aws.bedrock-agentcore"],
    "detail-type": ["API Call via AWS CloudTrail"],
    "detail": {"eventName": ["UpdateAgentRuntime"]}
}
events_client.put_rule(
    Name=f"{LAMBDA_NAME}-trigger",
    EventPattern=json.dumps(event_pattern),
    State="ENABLED",
)

清理

为避免持续产生费用，请在使用完毕后删除以下资源：

  • Lambda 函数 – 删除推送同步 Lambda 及其 IAM 执行角色。
  • Amazon EventBridge 规则 – 删除该规则及其 Lambda 目标。
  • AgentCore Identity – 删除工作负载身份和 OAuth2 凭证提供程序。
  • 注册表记录 – 删除或弃用测试 MCP 服务器记录。
  • 注册表 – 如果注册表仅为测试而创建，请将其删除。
  • （多账户）移除账户 B 中的跨账户 Amazon EventBridge 规则和资源策略。

你可以在示例代码仓库中找到清理代码。

已知限制与未来改进

此处介绍的示例代码（以及完整示例中的代码）可以从以下几个方面进行扩展：

  • 自动注册新的 MCP 服务器 – 目前，匹配的注册表记录必须预先存在。未来可以增强此功能，在首次检测到此前未知的 MCP 服务器时自动创建记录。
  • 手动“强制同步”触发器 – 对于时间敏感的部署，可以通过 Amazon API Gateway 或 CLI 命令提供按需调用路径，在常规 CloudTrail 投递流程之外传递变更。
  • 冷启动韧性 – 如果 MCP 服务器处于冷启动状态并返回零个工具，Lambda 目前不会重试。添加指数退避机制，并在工具数量为零时跳过更新，可以提高可靠性。

结论

AWS Agent Registry 为组织的 AI 智能体和 MCP 服务器提供了一个受治理且可被发现的目录。

推送同步 Lambda 模式弥补了信息更新不及时的问题：检测到服务器变更时，注册表记录会在“已知限制”部分所述的约束下，自动、安全地更新。更新会使记录回到 DRAFT 状态，记录必须经过审批工作流才能再次被发现。

当你的智能体规模从少量 MCP 服务器增长到数百台时，这种模式可以让注册表始终作为单一权威信息源，持续保持信息最新且经过审核。
